pass.answer: Run `/user-interface:design` on the layout first: its `web-layout` concern covers hierarchy, spacing and alignment, the usual cause when a screen looks off and you can't say why. Look at the result, then take the material concern (forms, if the page is mostly fields), and run `/user-interface:audit` before it ships.
pass.why: layout pass first, one concern now, later steps presented as coming after it

pass.answer: One skill for now: the design skill's layout and spacing pass (hierarchy, spacing, alignment). If the layout turns out right but unfinished, the next pass is layout stability; don't run both at once.
pass.why: layout pass first, a single skill now, the follow-up kept for later

fail.answer: Start with `/user-interface:audit` on the settings page; it will rank what is wrong with the layout, and then you can fix the findings.
fail.why: leads with a review instead of the layout pass

fail.answer: Run the layout pass in `/user-interface:design`, and at the same time run typography, color, forms, `/user-interface:write-css` and `/user-interface:audit` so everything is covered in one go.
fail.why: near miss: layout comes first, but five more skills and concerns run at the same time

fail.answer: Try `/prototype:explore-directions` to build three settings page layouts and pick the one you like.
fail.why: throwaway variants first, though the complaint is a layout that feels off
